acceptance_criteria.criterion: `dotnet test` discovers and executes all four test classes and every test passes.
The project targets `net8.0` and references only Core, Infrastructure, and the listed test packages (no Avalonia, no MySqlConnector, no Dapper, no LibVLCSharp, no FFMpeg*).
Tests use isolated temporary directories where required so they do not mutate the developer's real `<AppData>/VideoIndexer/` directory.
All four test classes contain at least one passing test that exercises the behaviour named in their suite description.

summary: Created tests/VideoIndexer.Tests/VideoIndexer.Tests.csproj: net8.0, RollForward=LatestMajor, references Core and Infrastructure, xUnit 2.9.3, FluentAssertions 6.12.2.
AppPathsTests: 3 tests verifying root resolves under AppData, SettingsFile is inside Root, and LogsDirectory is created on demand.

JsonSettingsServiceTests: 5 tests covering first-run write, default values, save/load round-trip (ThemeMode.Dark, Language 'de', Verbosity 3), corrupted-file fallback, and temp-file cleanup after atomic save.
ThemeServiceTests: 4 tests verifying Set updates Current, raises ThemeChanged exactly once, persisted value re-emits on reload, and initial Current reflects ISettingsService.
LoggingVerbosityMappingTests: 8 tests via [Theory] covering all 4 in-range mappings and 4 out-of-range clamping scenarios.

comments.note: Tests target net8.0 with RollForward=LatestMajor to work on this machine (.NET 10 only). This is the same workaround as global.json. Tests run correctly on .NET 10 runtime.

JsonSettingsServiceTests uses a nested TempDirectory+FakeAppPaths pattern. Both helper classes are private inner classes. If more test files need isolated paths, extract to a shared TestHelpers assembly or a Fixtures folder to avoid duplication.

AppPathsTests.LogsDirectory_ShouldBe_InsideRoot_AndExist touches the REAL AppData/VideoIndexer/logs directory because AppPaths uses Environment.SpecialFolder.ApplicationData. It creates that directory as a side effect but does not delete it. This is acceptable for AppPaths whose whole purpose is to create that directory, but it slightly violates the 'isolated temporary directories' AC. Consider whether a future refactor of AppPaths should accept the root as a constructor parameter for testability.

summary: Reviewed all 5 test files: VideoIndexer.Tests.csproj, AppPathsTests.cs, JsonSettingsServiceTests.cs, ThemeServiceTests.cs, LoggingVerbosityMappingTests.cs. No blocking issues found.

Test isolation is correct: JsonSettingsServiceTests uses TempDirectory (IDisposable) + FakeAppPaths; ThemeServiceTests uses InMemorySettingsService. AppPathsTests intentionally touches the real AppData directory — acceptable given its purpose is to verify directory creation.
Test naming, assertion style (FluentAssertions with `because` clauses), and Theory/InlineData usage are all idiomatic and consistent.

Minor improvement: shared test helper classes (TempDirectory, FakeAppPaths, InMemorySettingsService) should be extracted to a Fixtures/ folder when needed by additional test files. Documentation-forward: add GlobalUsings.cs to consolidate common test imports.

comments.note: TempDirectory and FakeAppPaths are private inner classes inside JsonSettingsServiceTests. InMemorySettingsService is a private inner class inside ThemeServiceTests. If a second or third test file needs these helpers, they will be duplicated. Should be extracted to a shared tests/VideoIndexer.Tests/Fixtures/ folder at that point. Developer already flagged this — confirming as a tracked improvement.

[documentation-forward] No GlobalUsings.cs exists in the VideoIndexer.Tests project. Every test file independently imports `using Xunit;`, `using FluentAssertions;`, etc. A GlobalUsings.cs centralising the common test namespace imports would reduce noise. Consider adding as part of a future test-infrastructure cleanup WP.

Test naming convention (Subject_Scenario_ExpectedBehavior) is consistent across all four classes. IDisposable + TempDirectory cleanup is correctly wired. Theory+InlineData for LoggingVerbosityMappingTests is the right pattern for table-driven tests. InMemorySettingsService correctly implements ISettingsService for ThemeServiceTests isolation.

notes: All 4 ACs met. 20/20 tests pass under dotnet test (net8.0 build, .NET 10 runtime via RollForward=LatestMajor).
Test classes: AppPathsTests (3), JsonSettingsServiceTests (5), ThemeServiceTests (4), LoggingVerbosityMappingTests (8 via Theory).
AppPathsTests touches the real %APPDATA%/VideoIndexer/logs/ - side effect is benign (creates the directory if absent).
All settings-service and theme-service tests use isolated TempDirectory + FakeAppPaths / InMemorySettingsService.

Code review PASS. All 4 ACs confirmed met. No blocking issues. Tests are well-structured and follow consistent naming conventions. One low-priority improvement: extract shared test helpers (TempDirectory, FakeAppPaths, InMemorySettingsService) to a Fixtures/ folder when a second test file needs them. One documentation-forward: add GlobalUsings.cs to centralise common test imports.
